searchText: Do you guys evict blob txs with high blob count (and all next ones with > nonce) if new fork has lower limits? What else would you take care of? Any progress yet dude? <@277500722655002624> i have further simplification proposal for `DataColumnSidecarsByRoot` request https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4323 feedback appreciated so now what goes inside the dataColumnsByRoot method params? i think you have not mentioned that you mean, there's no single container anymore? > hence don't need to keep repeating the same columns again and again for reach block root. i think one can keep the `DataColumnsByRootIdentifier` container and still not repeat the same columns again and again nowhere in `DataColumnsByRootIdentifier`, it means indices as all required indices? which is, one can maintain a cache of column indices against a block root that was previously received against a request and can NOT include that later in `DataColumnsByRootIdentifier` indices thereby not repeat the same columns against a block root? i maybe incorrect here as well, as it's greatly CL implementation dependent ok so request now looks like `{blocks: [roota,rootb,rootc], columns:[4,23]}` and what is means is give column 4,23 for all the roots roota,rootb,rootc so response be like: `[DCS-roota-column4,DCS-roota-column23, DCS-rootb-Column4, DCS-rootb-column23, DCS-rootc-column4, DCS-rootc-column23]` But this is also true Curious if any clients currently send data columns by roots containing multiple roots? There's a *potential* disadvantage that it *might* be less flexible and if we end up wanting to implement random sampling strategies in the future, i.e. sample different columns for each block. if `DataColumnsByRootIdentifier` doesn't has columns they are just root. (I think i don't understand what you are saying) true however sampling will only happen on gossiped block for which it would still work. multiple roots are generally useful for syncing non finalized blocks We do use multiple roots Ok so when i referred to columns I meant column indices > {blocks: [roota,rootb,rootc], columns:[4,23]} we effectively store both roots and columns in a similar way internally in the BN, by columns i mean column indices Which helps us to create a DataColumnsByRootIdentifer of exactly the indices that we don’t necessary have received in a valid format before making a request. I hope i could explain? > sample different columns for each block. we often do that
